_comment: Test Twin Propeller Aircraft - Top-level design REQUIREMENTS: what the aircraft must DO or what the preliminary design is required to assume. This file is read by MissionProfileReader and the sizing/constraint framework. Requirements are fidelity-independent and must not contain discipline-owned quantities such as CLmax, CD0, K, thrust lapse, TSFC, BSFC, or propeller efficiency. Aircraft/specification data belongs in the appropriate aircraft input/model files.
_cite: metabook = AE481 metabook worked Example 4.2, docs/reference_extracts/metabook_data.md; Roskam Table 3.1 etc. are the primary tables the metabook names. Constraint-class field names verified against src/constraints/{TakeoffFieldLengthConstraint, LandingFieldLengthConstraint, ClimbGradientConstraint, ExcessPowerConstraint, LevelFlightConstraint}.m.

geometry._comment: Preliminary geometry requirements/design assumptions. These are consumed by the sizing framework and are not owned by the geometry discipline model.

cruise._src: Cruise condition [metabook §4.11 Eq. 4.57] -- 8000 ft, KTAS >= 200. Consumed by the mission long-range cruise segment and the Cruise constraint.

_src_design_range_nmi: Design mission range 1,200 nmi. Fixed payload assumes single pilot crew and 5 additional passengers assumed to be 200 lb each. Not consumed directly by the constraint analysis; recorded so the requirement set is complete.

missions._comment: Mission PROFILES: the ordered segment sequence each mission flies. This is a fidelity-independent requirement. Each segment carries requirement data only; discipline-owned quantities such as CLmax, CD0, K, propeller efficiency, BSFC, and engine power come from the injected discipline models.
missions._cite: Mission-profile structure adapted from the existing aircraft requirements framework.

std_mission._description: Startup/taxi/takeoff (folded historical 0.970), climb (0.984), cruise 1,200 nmi (Breguet Eq. 2.7), 45-min loiter (Breguet endurance Eq. 2.16), descent (0.992), landing/taxi/shutdown (0.992). The 6% reserve_fuel_fraction [Eq. 2.17] (trapped fuel + additional reserve) is applied ON TOP of the full mission by MissionAnalysisBase -- it is separate from the 45-min design loiter above, so there is no double-count. Every physics/historical segment yields a fuel burn.
std_mission._cite_reserve_fuel_fraction: Wf/W0 = (1 - W_final/W0)*1.06 [metabook Eq. 2.17] -- the 6% covers reserve and trapped fuel. See the mission requirements documentation.
std_mission._src_cruise_distance_nm: Cruise range = 1,200 nmi [mission requirement]. Cruise KTAS 200 and altitude 8,000 ft. See Ttpa_requirements.md §5.2.
std_mission._src_loiter: 45-minute design loiter at 4,000 ft and 120 KTAS. The 6% reserve_fuel_fraction (Eq. 2.17, trapped fuel + additional reserve) still applies ON TOP of the full mission.
